title: Corinth
lead: A Roman colony on the isthmus of Greece and capital of the province of Achaia, refounded by Julius Caesar in 44 BC a century after Rome destroyed the old Greek city. Paul founded its church during a stay of about eighteen months (Acts 18), and his letters to it (1 and 2 Corinthians) are the fullest picture of an early church's life.

sections.b: The Greek city of Corinth controlled the trade across the isthmus and was destroyed by the Roman general Mummius in 146 BC. Julius Caesar refounded it as a Roman colony in 44 BC, and it quickly became the busiest city of Greece, with two ports, Lechaeum on the west and Cenchreae on the east. It hosted the Isthmian Games and was the seat of the proconsul of Achaia. Its reputation for vice comes largely from writers describing the older Greek city.
